newsitem.title: USA: Raytheon may seek US aid for mergers.
newsitem.headline: Raytheon may seek US aid for mergers.

text.p: Raytheon Co may ask U.S. taxpayers to pick up part of the costs associated with recent mergers, even as two congressmen try to end the government's reimbursement policy, The Boston Globe reported on Tuesday.

The Globe reported that Raytheon spokesman Robert McWade said it was too early to say whether the company would apply for reimbursements for its more recent acquisitions. McWade was not immediately available for comment on the report.
Lexington, Mass.-based Raytheon said it would spend $2.95 billion to acquire Texas Instruments, Inc.'s defense electronics unit and $9.5 billion for General Motors Corp's Hughes Aircraft.

Since 1993, the Defense Department has paid restructuring costs associated with the merger of defense contractors as an incentive for industry consolidation and elimination of excess overhead that was driving up prices for weapons systems.

Vermont's Independent Rep. Bernard Sanders introduced a bill to prevent the Pentagon from paying restructuring costs associated with the merger of Boeing Corp and McDonnell Douglas Corp. Rep. Chris Smith, R-N.J., also plans to introduce legislation that would block any Pentagon payments for merger associated costs, the newspaper said.
